current_news.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey
current_news.summary: TDI-Brooks has completed a geotechnical mission, bolstering Cook Inlet LNG’s efforts to shore up Southcentral Alaska’s energy supplies.
current_news.fact_excerpt:
October 22, 2026 · 34 minutes ago

U.S.-headquartered geotechnical and offshore survey research and service company TDI-Brooks has wrapped up a critical geotechnical campaign for Cook Inlet LNG, a strategic initiative designed to secure natural gas supplies for Southcentral Alaska, delivering vital subsurface data to support the project's anchor selection and helping bring the developer’s floating import terminal aspirations closer to reality.

TDI-Brooks has concluded a geotechnical project for the Cook Inlet LNG project (CI LNG) in Cook Inlet, Alaska, providing its Neptune N5K cone penetration testing (CPT) system for an anchor site characterization study. The work supported the project developer by collecting subsurface soil data to inform anchor selection.

According to the U.S. player, the study covered different locations within the project site with a scope of 16 CPTs in water depths ranging from 10 to 25 meters. Operations were conducted from the R/V Poseidon , a third-party vessel working in the region, demonstrating the firm’s ability to deploy specialized geotechnical equipment aboard locally available vessels.

The Cook Inlet LNG project is an energy security initiative designed to address declining natural gas reserves in the Cook Inlet basin of Southcentral Alaska to stave off a potential energy shortfall for heating and electricity by serving as a near-term bridge solution to import gas.

window_news.title: Cheniere Signs Long-Term Sale and Purchase Agreements to Supply QatarEnergy with LNG through 2054
window_news.summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries,…
window_news.fact_excerpt:
HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries, Sabine Pass Liquefaction, LLC (“SPL”) and Corpus Christi Liquefaction, LLC (“CCL”), have each entered into long-term liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) sale and purchase agreements (“SPA”) with QatarEnergy to supply a total of 4 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG through 2054.

Through Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. (NYSE: CQP), we are developing an expansion of the existing Sabine Pass Liquefaction Project (“SPL Project”) with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG (the “SPL Expansion Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities, which would grow the total production capacity of the SPL Project to over 50 mtpa of LNG. We expect to execute the SPL Expansion Project in a phased approach. The first phase is expected to include a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal, and has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. In May 2026, the lump sum, turnkey engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract with Bechtel Energy, Inc. (“Bechtel”) for the first phase of the SPL Expansion Project was signed, and Bechtel was released to commence early engineering and procurement under a limited notice to proceed (LNTP).

window_news.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
window_news.summary: Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.
window_news.fact_excerpt:
October 22, 2026 · 2 minutes ago

Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.

Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

Jackdaw has the potential to deliver around 6% of projected UK North Sea gas production, which is considered to be enough fuel to heat the equivalent of 1.4 million homes at a time when older gas fields are reaching the end of their production.

The field, located approximately 250 kilometers east of Aberdeen, is expected to be among the lowest-emission developments on the UK Continental Shelf (UKCS), while supporting jobs and bolstering Britain’s energy security.

The field is located in the Central North Sea (CNS), 30 kilometers southeast of the Shearwater platform and adjacent to the UK/Norway median line. Jackdaw is a gas/condensate development comprising a not permanently attended wellhead platform with four wells, tied back to the Shearwater hub via a 31-kilometer pipeline.

While the latest approval marks a major turning point, the environmental battles are not entirely over since environmental groups like Greenpeace remain strongly opposed to the development of the North Sea oil and gas projects, which have become a primary battleground for climate litigation.

Responding to the government giving the Jackdaw gas field the go-ahead, Sam Richards , CEO of Britain Remade, said: “Britain is going to need gas for decades to come, as even the Climate Change Committee recognises. The choice is not between gas and no gas, but between gas produced in British waters and gas shipped in from abroad at higher cost and with higher emissions.

政策与能源安全.title: Norway set on tapping into Arctic gas potential: New study to unlock 1988 Barents Sea discovery
政策与能源安全.summary: Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea.
政策与能源安全.fact_excerpt:
Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea.

Decades after being left behind in the frozen depths of the High North, a forgotten 1980s gas find in the Barents Sea is getting a second look. As Europe hungers for new energy sources and low-carbon reserves, Norway is launching a fresh push to unlock the untapped potential of the Arctic, starting with a neglected discovery 200 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle.

The Barents Sea is home to a number of discoveries that could hold vast volumes of gas but remains less explored than other parts of the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), with several discoveries in these waters potentially containing significant volumes of gas, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate, which emphasizes that a new study could uncover major opportunities for one of these discoveries.

The gas discovery that this study will aim to gain more insight into is Norselhøgda (the well 7226/11-1 ), which is situated about 200 kilometers north of Hammerfest and was made in 1988. The discovery was production-tested, but the acreage was subsequently relinquished to the authorities.

Several comparable discoveries have been made in the area, which include production license 1313 , located to the north of the Norselhøgda discovery and awarded in APA 2025 . The Gro discovery in the Norwegian Sea is another discovery the Norwegian Offshore Directorate hopes to revive, along with the Linerle discovery in the Norwegian Sea.

SundaGas Banda Unipessoal, a wholly owned subsidiary of the UK-based and AIM-listed Sunda Energy, has dodged a bullet in Timor-Leste with a crucial 12-month reprieve, since the regulatory extension keeps hopes alive for the long-awaited appraisal well following a termination warning earlier this year over missed deadlines, as partner negotiations heat up.

Sunda Energy’s subsidiary has received from Autoridade Nacional do Petróleo (ANP), Timor-Leste’s upstream regulator, an extension of 12 months to the current phase of the production sharing contract (PSC) TL-SO-19-16, which contains the Chuditch gas field, where SundaGas has been preparing to drill the Chuditch-2 appraisal well. The firm operates this asset in partnership with its government-owned joint venture partner, Timor Gap Chuditch Unipessoal .

The extension granted by ANP allows the joint venture time to continue the discussions, with a stated timeline for completion prior to the end of 2026. Sunda explains that this extension is subject to a suspension of the uplift on the cost recovery account for the PSC from June 19, 2024, until such time as drilling operations on Chuditch-2 have started.

The firm is continuing to liaise with Finder under the framework of the letter of intent announced in April 2026 with respect to collaboration between the planned drilling campaigns for KTJ and Chuditch-2 drilling campaigns.

LNG供应与流向.title: FERC comes up with three-tiered fast track plan to streamline US LNG permitting
LNG供应与流向.summary: FERC has proposed an LNG blanket authorization program to slash red tape, optimize permitting, and fast-track U.S. energy infrastructure development.
LNG供应与流向.fact_excerpt:
FERC’s notice of proposed rulemaking (NOPR) intends to establish an LNG blanket authorization program to allow eligible activities at LNG facilities to proceed without case-specific authorization orders under Sections 3 and 7 of the Natural Gas Act (NGA). This program is modeled on the commission’s 40-year blanket certificate program for interstate natural gas pipelines.

Laura V. Swett , FERC’s Chairman, commented: “American energy dominance requires us to build and maintain the energy infrastructure our country needs without unnecessary delay. I am immensely proud of FERC’s historic proposal.

Under the automatic authorization umbrella are activities that would not increase an LNG plant’s authorized capacity, expand the authorized vertical or horizontal extents within the plant’s footprint, or cause flows, levels, volumes, pressures, temperatures, compositions, or loads to exceed applicable design limits.

A 60-day prior notice covers activities that may increase the plant’s authorized capacity but remain within the plant’s footprint and do not cause operating conditions to exceed the design limits of the affected or remaining facilities.

A 90-day prior notice entails construction of new LNG facilities, such as liquefaction trains, LNG tanks, and marine berths, and related auxiliary systems, including those located outside the plant’s footprint, subject to limitations on facility type, location, and size.

Técnicas Reunidas, a Spanish-based engineering contractor, is cementing its footprint in North America, with an engineering, procurement and construction management (EPCM) assignment worth more than €200 million for Phase 2 of the Coastal GasLink pipeline awarded by LNG Canada, a joint venture featuring Shell, Petronas, PetroChina, Mitsubishi Corporation, and KOGAS.

CGL Phase 2 will be delivered through an integrated execution model, with LNG Canada leading project construction as Phase 2 Execution Manager and TR Canada E&C providing the EPCM services, while CGL will remain the owner, operator, and permit holder of the pipeline and associated facilities.

The contract award comes only weeks after LNG Canada reached its Phase 2 final investment decision (FID) to advance the next stage of development of this British Columbia-based project of national significance.

The project includes the construction of five additional compressor stations, as well as modifications to both existing and planned facilities at various points along the pipeline route.

The newly awarded contract with LNG Canada adds to the company’s extensive experience in midstream projects, which includes 30,000 kilometers of oil and gas pipelines and more than 35 large compression projects worldwide.

其他天然气新闻.title: Nordic energy players hit paydirt with new gas and condensate discovery
其他天然气新闻.summary: Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.
其他天然气新闻.fact_excerpt:
Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.

Norway’s energy duo, Vår Energi and Equinor, have made a gas and condensate find in a new Norwegian Sea license, uncovering a fresh prospect estimated to hold up to 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).

Vår Energi and Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery in the 6407/5-3 S well, which is known as the Lakris prospect in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace in the Norwegian Sea.

The water depth at the site is 218 meters. The well, which was not formation-tested, but data and samples were collected, will now be permanently plugged and abandoned.

The well 6407/5-3 S encountered gas and condensate in the upper Tilje Formation in heterolithic reservoir rocks, totalling 54 meters, with moderate to poor reservoir quality. The gas/water contact was not encountered in the well.

其他天然气新闻.summary: This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.
其他天然气新闻.fact_excerpt:
This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.

A gas project off the coast of Libya, which is operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas Libyan Branch, a consortium formed by National Oil Corporation (NOC) of Libya and Eni North Africa, is anticipated to stop decades of costly flaring in its tracks, capturing hundreds of millions of cubic meters of gas to fuel local power plants and feed European export pipelines.

The recovered gas will be supplied to the domestic market, providing an incremental production of around 700 million standard cubic meters per year, helping meet demand from the power generation sector.

In addition, the project will support additional gas volumes available for export to Europe through the GreenStream pipeline. Saipem finished the lifting operations of the gas recovery module for the BGUP earlier this year.

The pre-commissioning activities were planned for approximately 28 kilometers of already laid subsea pipelines to connect the DP3, DP4, and Sabratha platforms to enable the transportation of the recovered gas to the Mellitah treatment complex.

This agreement establishes a forward-looking framework for both organizations to leverage their respective strengths and pursue opportunities across the energy value chain, spanning upstream development, gas and LNG, and downstream opportunities, as well as low-carbon solutions.

Petronas has been present in Vietnam since 1991, when it made its first investment in the country’s upstream sector as a pioneer international investor in Vietnam’s oil and gas industry.

其他天然气新闻.title: Completing electrification project at Troll
其他天然气新闻.summary: The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
其他天然气新闻.fact_excerpt:
The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

The Troll licence partnership has informed the Norwegian Ministry of Energy that the Troll West Electrification (TWEL) project will be completed after commissioning the first electric export compressor on Troll C, and without installing the second electric export compressor on Troll C, as originally planned in the 2021 plan for development and operation (PDO).

The decision also helps maintain high and stable gas supplies to Europe at a time when energy security remains important. It is expected to make around 2.3 billion standard cubic metres of additional gas available to the European market in 2027 and 2028. This corresponds to approximately two years of gas consumption for around one million European households.

Troll A became the first platform on the Norwegian continental shelf to receive power from shore in 1996. Troll B and Troll C were partially electrified in 2024. TWEL has reduced emissions from the Troll area by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year, corresponding to approximately 75% of the emission reductions originally planned in the PDO (440,000 tonnes per year). This makes the project one of the largest emissions reduction measures on the Norwegian continental shelf. Overall, the measures have reduced emissions from the Troll area to approximately the same level as in 1999.
